Corned Beef and Cabbage

Served at: Saint Patrick's Day

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 3-4 hours

Corned Beef and Cabbage is the quintessential dish for Saint Patrick's Day celebrations in the United States. While not traditionally Irish, this hearty meal became a staple for Irish immigrants, offering a delicious and comforting way to honor their heritage. It's a flavorful one-pot dish perfect for feeding a crowd.

Ingredients

  • 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) corned beef brisket with spice packet
  • 1 large onion, quartered
  • 4-5 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks
  • 4-5 medium potatoes, peeled and quartered (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)
  • 1 small head of green cabbage, cut into 6-8 wedges
  • 6 cups (1.4 liters) water or beef broth
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) apple cider vinegar (optional)
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Remove the corned beef brisket from its packaging and rinse it thoroughly under cold water to remove excess salt. Place the brisket in a large pot or Dutch oven.
  2. Sprinkle the contents of the spice packet over the brisket. Add the quartered onion, carrots, and potatoes around the beef.
  3. Pour in the water or beef broth, ensuring the beef is mostly submerged. Add the apple cider vinegar, if using.
  4. Bring the liquid to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the corned beef is fork-tender.
  5. During the last 30-45 minutes of cooking, add the cabbage wedges to the pot, nestling them into the broth around the beef and other vegetables. Continue to simmer until the cabbage is tender-crisp.
  6. Once cooked, carefully remove the corned beef from the pot and let it rest on a cutting board for 10-15 minutes before slicing. Slice the corned beef against the grain for maximum tenderness.
  7. Arrange the sliced corned beef, cabbage, carrots, and potatoes on a large platter. Drizzle with some of the cooking liquid, if desired, and garnish with fresh parsley. Serve hot.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, you can add a bottle of dark beer (like Guinness) to the cooking liquid along with the water or broth.
  • Leftovers make excellent sandwiches, especially on rye bread with mustard.
  • Adjust cooking time for vegetables; add them later if you prefer them firmer.
